\section[l'applicazione]{l'applicazione — the app, the application; the effort}

\label{lesson:IT-C400-applicazione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to log in, then the Italian for to sign up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'applicazione}
\textbf{l'applicazione} — \textquotedblleft{}the app, the application; the effort\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Con questa applicazione puoi pagare il parcheggio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{With this app you can pay for parking.}
\end{quote}

In speech, often \emph{l'app}. It also means diligence: \emph{studiare con applicazione}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{applicazione} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{applicātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a joining to, an attaching\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{applicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to attach\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{plicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to fold\textquotedblright{}; the software sense came from English.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'applicazione}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'applicazione}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'applicazione}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to log in, then the Italian for to sign up, then say \emph{l'applicazione} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'applicazione mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The app, the application; the effort\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[installare]{installare — to install}

\label{lesson:IT-C400-installare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to sign up, then the Italian for the app.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: installare}
\textbf{installare} — \textquotedblleft{}to install\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se installi l'aggiornamento, il telefono va più veloce.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If you install the update, the phone runs faster.}
\end{quote}

Also to fit something in a house: \emph{installare una lampada}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{installare} was borrowed from French \emph{installer}, from Medieval Latin \emph{installāre} \textquotedblleft{}to put in a stall, to seat in office\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{stallum}, a word of Germanic origin; compare Old High German \emph{stal} \textquotedblleft{}place, stall\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{installare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{installare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{installare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to sign up, then the Italian for the app, then say \emph{installare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does installare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To install\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[disinstallare]{disinstallare — to uninstall}

\label{lesson:IT-C400-disinstallare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the app, then the Italian for to install.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: disinstallare}
\textbf{disinstallare} — \textquotedblleft{}to uninstall\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se un'app non ti serve, disinstallala.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If you do not need an app, uninstall it.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Dis-} reverses the verb.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{disinstallare} is built from \emph{dis-} \textquotedblleft{}un-\textquotedblright{} and \emph{installare}, which was borrowed from French \emph{installer}, from Medieval Latin \emph{installāre} \textquotedblleft{}to put in a stall\textquotedblright{}, on a Germanic word for a place; compare Old High German \emph{stal} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{disinstallare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{disinstallare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{disinstallare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the app, then the Italian for to install, then say \emph{disinstallare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does disinstallare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To uninstall\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[il dispositivo]{il dispositivo — the device}

\label{lesson:IT-C400-dispositivo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to install, then the Italian for to uninstall.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il dispositivo}
\textbf{il dispositivo} — \textquotedblleft{}the device\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Puoi usare l'app su tre dispositivi.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You can use the app on three devices.}
\end{quote}

Phones, tablets and computers. Also a safety device: \emph{un dispositivo di sicurezza}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dispositivo} is modelled on French \emph{dispositif}, built on Latin \emph{dispositus} \textquotedblleft{}arranged\textquotedblright{}, past participle of \emph{dispōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to set in order\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), on \emph{pōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to put\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il dispositivo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il dispositivo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to install, then the Italian for to uninstall, then say \emph{il dispositivo} again
\end{itemize}

\section[il software]{il software — the software}

\label{lesson:IT-C400-software}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to uninstall, then the Italian for the device.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il software}
\textbf{il software} — \textquotedblleft{}the software\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il software è nuovo e ancora non lo conosco.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The software is new and I do not know it yet.}
\end{quote}

Masculine, invariable. \emph{L'hardware} is the machine itself.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{software} was borrowed from English \emph{software} (EtymDB), built from \emph{soft} and \emph{ware} \textquotedblleft{}goods\textquotedblright{}, on the model of \emph{hardware}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
